STEP 1 - Vessel type: The vessel is a square flat plate. It has a flat white centre with a raised rim band and no visible inner wall or bowl shadow.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks like a medium-large dinner plate, roughly 24-26 cm across.
b) Reference cue: the carrot pieces are about 5-6 cm long. The plate spans roughly 4.5-5 carrot lengths across the width (about 330 px of plate width versus ~60-70 px per carrot length), giving about 24-27 cm.
Reconciled width: about 25 cm square (625 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Carrots (cooked, sliced/chunky pieces): the carrots cover roughly 35% of the plate area, about 220 cm². They form a mound about 2 pieces deep at the centre, with a peak of about 2.5-3 cm and an average of about 1.5 cm.
  Volume = 220 x 1.5 = 330 ml. Bulk density for chopped vegetables = 0.6 g/ml, so 330 x 0.6 ≈ 200 g.
- Scattered single carrot slices on the rim (about 3-4 pieces) are included in the estimate above.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No base layer (rice, sauce, greens) is visible. The carrots appear glazed, but the sauce is only a thin smear (negligible). No additional items.

STEP 5 - Energy: Cooked carrots are about 35-40 kcal per 100 g. Glaze or butter adds a little, so I use 45 kcal/100 g as served.

Total: about 200 g, about 90 kcal.
